problem: The island has sparse primitive scenery, an overly regular coast, indistinct locations and inaccessible-looking entrances. Island and billiards expose touch and keyboard hints simultaneously. Improve the actual playable world, preserve saves, and share one live input-context owner.
reuseDecision: Extend the existing island blueprint, movement, scene and interior owners rather than adding a second world or router. Share browser input modality in game-shell, independently of viewport size, and compose it into the existing joystick and billiards presentation. Native Pointer Events and matchMedia provide the required capability without a device-detection package. Follow the existing asset-review workflow pattern for inspecting the official Kenney CC0 archive before selecting, pinning and integrating assets. Review artifacts retain the exact tracked source for reproducibility; no workflow writes source back to branches.
nonGoals: Changing billiards physics or network protocols
Erasing player progress or silently regenerating saved islands
Copying Nintendo assets, branding or exact scenes
Publishing unvalidated changes to stable or relaxing budgets to hide regressions
acceptance: Imported assets have verified provenance, explicit license, hashes and bounded runtime cost; no runtime CDN dependency
Land generation and walkability share a deterministic boundary, keep routes and entrances accessible and support bounded shallow-water walking
Houses and cave can be entered and exited using normal player controls; saved progress survives
Forest, beach and interiors have distinct smoothly transitioning presentation
Touch, pen and keyboard/mouse input update both games without reload; resizing alone never guesses input modality
Device context listeners are shared and released; gestures survive or cancel safely on focus loss and route disposal
Types, domain tests, ownership, asset checks and existing bundle ratchets pass
Actual browser interaction and screenshot evidence cover mobile, desktop and hybrid input, including the existing failing island walk fixture
